questions.subject: Reading
questions.learningObjective: Relate a written description to locations in a diagram and extract the words that label them.
questions.passage:
Showing letters under controlled conditions

A local archive wanted to exhibit historic letters without exposing them to the rapid changes in humidity that occurred in the gallery. Staff chose a small cabinet whose front panel could be opened for occasional inspection. They designed the cabinet so that the visitor would see only the letters and their support, with most of the working components concealed.

A narrow light strip sits high inside the front of the cabinet. From this position it lights the display rather than shining directly towards the visitor. The pressure seal runs down the front closing edge. When the panel is shut, the seal compresses into a thin band and limits the exchange of air with the gallery.

Below the display platform, a shallow buffer tray holds material that absorbs or releases moisture as conditions change. The placement allows staff to remove the tray without moving the letters. The upper display space and the lower service space communicate through small openings at the platform edge.

To monitor conditions, a cable from a measuring instrument passes out through a sensor port halfway up the rear wall. Staff can read the instrument from outside and decide when to investigate further. They still check the cabinet itself at scheduled intervals because a stable reading alone does not reveal whether every part of the display is in good condition.

stimulus.title: Cross-section of an archive display cabinet
stimulus.textAlternative: Side section. Left is front. A points to a narrow horizontal element high inside the front. B points to a band along the front closing edge. C points to a shallow component beneath the display platform. D points to a small fitting halfway up the rear wall.

questions.prompt: Identify the element marked A high inside the cabinet. Use no more than two words from the passage.
questions.explanation: The second paragraph places the light strip high inside the front.
